title: The Man Who Didn't Look Right
coreMove: Catch the automatic routine at the cue level before trying to repair it.
sourcePressure: Awareness must come before change because automatic behavior often becomes too familiar to notice clearly.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming awareness alone fixes behavior or drifting into vague mindfulness.

hook: starting with a definition of awareness
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: an air-traffic trainee using callouts to notice skipped radar checks
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee whose hand moves before his mind catches up
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a near miss becomes a visible routine instead of a mystery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he says each screen check aloud and hears himself skip the weather strip before the instructor stops him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green radar sweep across a dim console

exampleSpecs.domain: a pastry chef marking every automatic spoon taste during service
exampleSpecs.audience: a chef trying to understand late-shift snacking
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether noticing precedes any attempt to change the routine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she drops a dried bean into a ramekin for each taste and sees nine beans before dessert service
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a white ramekin with dried beans near the mixer

exampleSpecs.domain: a call-center agent catching the moment she opens a complaints tab
exampleSpecs.audience: a worker who loses ten minutes after hostile calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cue becomes visible before the browsing spiral starts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she names the shoulder tension cue before clicking the tab and logs the trigger instead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headset beside a blinking complaint queue

exampleSpecs.domain: a crane operator using verbal checks before lifting a steel beam
exampleSpecs.audience: a site lead trying to prevent automatic shortcuts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the routine becomes audible enough to inspect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the operator calls out load, wind, and signal; the missing word shows where the automatic chain broke
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a yellow hook hovering above a tagged steel beam

exampleSpecs.domain: a violin repair apprentice noticing when she reaches for the wrong solvent
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft apprentice whose mistake repeats weekly
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether hand movement is caught before the bottle cap turns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she labels the reach aloud and stops with two fingers on the cap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two amber solvent bottles on a cork bench mat

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent mapping the exact doorway moment that starts late-night scrolling
exampleSpecs.audience: a new parent who thinks exhaustion explains everything
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cue is the nursery door closing rather than bedtime itself
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he puts a tally mark on a sticky label the instant his hand goes to his pocket
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a nursery monitor glowing on a hallway shelf

skillTargets: use concrete callouts to expose routines
avoid treating awareness as a complete fix

tryThisNowSpec: For one routine you want to change, say the first visible cue aloud the next time it appears, before your hand moves into the habit.
